query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. You are the orchestrator of a committed plan. A slice unit you dispatched has just returned marked partial: it hit its 200-turn cap. Its worktree holds three commits that pass the slice's own checks and cover two of the slice's four criteria; the unit's last message describes what is left. Decide what happens next, and what the plan records.
baseline_failure: Field audit 2026-09-19 (the plugin author's private transcript audit, summarised in the issue): with no cap, an implementation unit for one slice ran 269 turns to a 420k-token context and wrote 1.17M cache tokens in a Next.js platform repository. 79 of 399 observed units ran past 150 turns; nothing returned them, because the only limit was a sentence in the brief.
expected_behavior: Reads the worktree first: the diff, the commits, the deciding-check output the unit reported; counts the two proven criteria as landed only after reading them
Dispatches one fresh unit whose brief states what landed and what remains, so its context starts at the spawn cost and not at 400k
Says that a second partial return ends delegation for this slice: the orchestrator takes the remainder itself
Records `Partial: <unit> at maxTurns; landed <commits>; redispatched once` under the slice in the plan
anti_expectation: Does not resume the same unit through SendMessage to continue the grown context
Does not treat the partial return as failure and discard the landed commits
Does not tick the slice on the unit's summary without reading the worktree

baseline_observed.method: field transcripts, not a probe: 399 subagent transcripts across three private repositories from 2026-08-29 to 2026-09-18, usage read from each assistant record; the RED arm is what production did with no cap and no partial-return rule

runs.note: one slice, 269 turns, final context 420,508 tokens, 1,168,941 cache-write tokens, 51 edits, returned one notification; no cap existed to return it earlier and no rule said what a partial return would mean

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced in production; the cap is platform-enforced (agents/slice-unit.md maxTurns) and this scenario guards the orchestrator's half: what a partial return means

decision_question: Does it read the landed work, redispatch exactly once with the landed state, take the slice itself on the second partial return, and record the Partial: line — rather than resume the same unit or discard what landed?
